You are a strict medical transcript verifier.
The transcript is numbered, one sentence per line: [0] ..., [1] ..., etc.
For each question, determine if it is established by the transcript.
Answer NO when information is absent or for near misses (different drug, dose, unit, duration, frequency, result).
For YES, cite ONLY the sentence IDs that support it, e.g. YES [2,3]. A single sentence is YES [5].
Sentence IDs are the ONLY allowed citation format. Free-text quotes are FORBIDDEN — never copy transcript text.
Output each answer on a new line formatted exactly as:
1. YES [2,3]
2. NO
...

NUMBERED TRANSCRIPT (one sentence per line):
[0] Morning, Dr.
[1] Scove.
[2] Thanks for fitting me in.
[3] Morning, Jens.
[4] Always good to see you.
[5] Busy out there with the school holidays?
[6] Very.
[7] The whole town seems to be on the move.
[8] It is like that every summer.
[9] So, what can I do for you?
[10] I need my ibumetin renewed.
[11] All right.
[12] And you are still taking pantoprazole alongside it?
[13] Yes, every day with it.
[14] Good.
[15] Now, one thing I want to be open with you about.
[16] You have used anti -inflammatory painkillers heavily and for a long time.
[17] Is that harming me?
[18] It means we should monitor your blood pressure and your kidney function.
[19] That is the sensible step.
[20] How do we go about that?
[21] I would like you to measure your blood pressure at home over three days.
[22] I can do that.
[23] And the kidneys?
[24] Blood tests.
[25] Please book a time for those.
[26] We check kidneys, cholesterol, and blood sugar.
[27] And you will still renew the ibumetin today?
[28] Yes.
[29] The prescription is created.
[30] Does that plan sound workable to you?
[31] It does.
[32] Home readings for three days, then the blood tests.
[33] That is it.
[34] Have you read anything good lately?
[35] I finished a crime novel last night.
[36] It kept me up far too late.
[37] The good ones tend to.
[38] Take care, Jens.
[39] Thanks.
[40] See you.

QUESTIONS:
1. Should kidney function be monitored?
2. Is there any reference to the patient planning a specific fitness challenge?
3. Did the patient ask for a renewal of the Ibumetin prescription?
4. Has the Ibumetin prescription been issued?
5. Is the patient also taking Pantoprazole?
6. Were liver values the focus of the planned blood tests?
7. Should the blood pressure readings be taken at the clinic instead of at home?
8. Will the blood tests include cholesterol and blood sugar?
9. Does the doctor consider the NSAID use long-standing and high?
10. Was blood pressure to be measured at home over three days?

ANSWERS:
